newsitem.title: CHINA: City Telecom seen raising HK$180 million in IPO.
newsitem.headline: City Telecom seen raising HK$180 million in IPO.

text.p: Calling services provider City Telecom (HK) Ltd is expected to issue about 100 million new shares to raise about HK$180 million in an initial public offer (IPO) in Hong Kong, market sources said on Thursday.

The new shares are expected to be priced at HK$1.80 each, giving a prospective price to earnings multiple of about seven to eight times, but no concrete listing details were immediately available to the market, sources said.

"From the proceeds, about HK$30 million is expected to be used to set up a switching station in Hong Kong, HK$40 million to build up networks in Hong Kong and Japan, with the balance going to working capital," one source said.
Dealing in the company's shares is expected to begin in early August. Citicorp International is seen to be the sponsor of the issue, sources said.
City Telecom is a seller of international calling services in Hong Kong. Its callback services covers more than 200 countries worldwide.
Callback services let customers make international phone calls via another country with cheaper charges.
The company forecast a profit of about HK$80 million for the year ending in August 31, 1997, up from HK$64 million in 1996, HK$19 million in 1995 and HK$13 million in 1994, sources said.
"It posted HK$30 million profit for the six months to February 1997 with turnover of HK$294 million," one source said.
Turnover was HK$500 million in 1996, up from HK$269 million in 1995, and HK$114 million in 1994, they said.
